title: Quotes: the basics
summary: The Quotes list, quote numbers and statuses, and how a quote goes from draft to accepted.

body.text: The **Quotes** page is where you build, price and send every quote. Each one gets a number like **Q-1234**. The list shows only the latest version of each quote; earlier versions are kept in its version history.
Reading the list

Each row shows the customer, the lead it belongs to (if any), the total including VAT, the status, the date it's valid until, and who created it. Click a **Q-number** to open the quote; click the customer or lead to go to them.
Statuses

rows: Being prepared. You can change anything.
The customer has it. It's fixed — to change it, create a revision.
The customer said yes. Its lead is marked won and the deal moves to Deliveries.
The customer said no. You can create a revision with a better offer.
Called off, with a reason. Nothing is deleted.

body.text: A quote can also be **superseded** (replaced by a revision) or **signed** (signed online by the customer). Both are permanently read-only, so the record of what the customer saw never changes.
Starting a quote

items: Press **New quote**.
Choose the customer and, if there is one, the lead under **Link to a lead (optional)**.
Add lines and any fees, then save.

body.text: You can also start a quote from a lead with **Create quote** — the lead's product is already on it.
Deleting a quote

**Delete quote** moves it to Trash, where it can be restored for **60 days**. Deleting an accepted quote reopens its lead if no other accepted quote is left. To call off a quote but keep it on record, use **Cancel quote** instead.

title: Building and pricing a quote
summary: Add products and your own lines, discounts, fees and delivery, a deposit, and choose how VAT is shown.

body.text: The quote editor has four tabs: **Build**, **Preview**, **Versions** and **Send**. You put the quote together on **Build**; the total on the right updates as you go.
Lines

items: **Product line** — pick a product from your catalogue. Its name and price fill in. If it comes in colours, set the **Colour preference**.
**Custom line** — type your own description and price for anything not in the catalogue.

body.text: Each line has a quantity, a **Unit price** and an optional discount (**Disc %**, 0–100). The line total is after the discount.
Fees and delivery

items: Under **Fees & delivery**, add a **Delivery** or **Fee** line.
Give it a **Label**, for example "Delivery to the coast".
Enter the amount. VAT is added at your workspace's rate.

body.text: Quote settings

items: **Valid until** — when the offer expires. It starts at your usual number of days, set under **Settings → Quotes**.
**Pricing basis** — **Prices include VAT** (the usual) or **Add VAT on top**.
**Deposit** — none, a percentage of the total, or a fixed amount. The total, deposit and **Balance on delivery** are all shown.
**Terms** — the terms printed on the quote. Your standard terms are filled in from **Settings → Quotes**.

body.text: Your VAT rate and currency are set under **Settings → Quotes**. If your workspace uses more than one currency, a quote can be in the customer's currency.
Check the **Preview** tab before sending — it shows exactly what the customer will see.
Every total — on screen, on the printed quote, invoice and agreement — is worked out the same way, so a discount shows the same everywhere.

title: Sending, accepting and revising quotes
summary: Mark a quote sent, record the customer's answer, and change a sent quote safely with a revision.

body.text: Once a quote leaves draft it's fixed — a customer must never see a quote change after they've received it. To change a sent or declined quote, you create a **revision**.
Sending

On the **Send** tab, check **Ready to send** and mark it sent. This fixes the version at the exact price the customer received. A quote needs at least one line first. To have it signed online, press **Continue to signing** — see **Getting a quote signed online**.
Recording the customer's answer

items: **Accepted** — records the sale and marks the lead won. Anything set to happen on a win runs, and a referral reward becomes due if the deal came through a referral. A quote out for signing must have its signing request voided first.
**Declined** — the customer said no.
**Back to draft** — reopens this version for editing.

body.text: If you move a quote out of accepted and its lead has no other accepted quote, the lead reopens, so it no longer counts as a sale.
Creating a revision

items: Open the sent or declined quote.
Press **Create revision**. Everything is copied into a new draft with a new Q-number, and the editor switches to it.
The original is marked superseded and kept, read-only, for the record.

body.text: Cancelling or copying

**Cancel quote** works on any quote, even a signed one, and asks for a reason. It leaves Deliveries, any signing request still with the customer is withdrawn, and stock set aside for it is released. Nothing is deleted — the signed copy and the history stay. **Duplicate** copies a quote into a new, unsigned draft — handy for starting again from a signed or cancelled quote.
A quote can't be edited while a signing link is out, once it's signed, once it's superseded, or once it has left draft. Withdraw the signing request or create a revision to change it.
Versions and change requests

Every version shown to a customer stays on record. The **Versions** tab lists them. If a customer asks for changes online, a banner on the quote shows their note, with a shortcut to create a revision.

title: Quote documents, printing and handover
summary: Print a quote, produce the invoice and sales agreement, and follow an accepted quote through to delivery.

body.text: Printing and documents

items: **Print / PDF** — on any quote.
**Invoice** and **Sales agreement** — once the quote is accepted.
**Generate** — owners can create any of your document templates for this quote and file it with the customer's documents.

body.text: Following the sale through
An accepted quote shows a **Fulfilment** strip: **Invoiced**, **Deposit paid**, **Delivery scheduled** and **Delivered**. Each turns green when done. A link takes you to the Deliveries board.
Delivery photos

items: Open the accepted quote.
In **Delivery photos**, choose one or more pictures — your phone's camera works.
Press **Upload**. The photos are filed on the customer and the quote.

title: Managing deliveries and handovers
summary: Get paid, book the delivery and hand over each sale on the Deliveries board.

body.text: The **Deliveries** board follows every sale from acceptance to handover. A quote appears the moment it's accepted and sits in the column for the step it hasn't done yet. After handover it stays in **Delivered this month** until the month ends.

rows: Invoice it, then take the deposit
Hand it over on the day
Handed over — kept here until the month ends

body.text: Working a card
Each card shows where things stand and **one** next step. Everything else — print links, corrections, Xero, transport bookings — is under **Details**.

items: **Awaiting payment — the invoice.** With Xero connected, press **Send invoice to Xero**; Xero's PDF is filed as the invoice. Without Xero, attach the invoice and press **Mark invoiced**.

**Awaiting payment — the deposit.** With Xero, press **Refresh** once the customer has paid and the deposit is picked up from Xero, or **Record the deposit by hand** with the proof of payment. Without Xero, attach the proof of payment and press **Deposit paid**.
**Ready to schedule.** Pick the date (and attach a file if you like) and press **Schedule delivery**.

**Scheduled.** Press **Open handover**, then **Complete delivery** (or **Review, sign & complete** where a guided handover is set up) to record who handed over and the handover checklist. Then press **Customer signs on this device**: the customer reads the delivery note and signs on screen, and the signed note is filed with the quote. Add delivery photos from the same card.

body.text: **Print delivery note** is under **Details** once a delivery is scheduled. If stock has been set aside for the sale, the card shows the unit's readiness (allocated, in pre-delivery inspection, or ready) and links to it.
Totals, what's been paid and what's still owed are on the **Invoices** page, where each row's **Payments** button records payments and opens the customer's statement.
The buttons on each card need the **Manage delivery milestones, files and handover** permission. Without it you can see the board but not change it.

title: Monthly targets and progress
summary: This month's goals for new leads, sales, deliveries and services, and how close the team is.

body.text: The **Targets** page shows this month's goals and how the team is doing. Each has a progress bar that turns green when the target is reached.

rows: The value of leads won this month

body.text: Each card shows the actual figure and, where a target is set, the target and the percentage reached. If no target is set, the card says so.
Everyone can see progress. Owners set the targets — see **Setting this month's targets**.

title: Setting this month's targets
summary: Owners set the month's goals for new leads, sales value, deliveries and services.

items: Open the **Targets** page.
Under **Set this month's targets**, enter a figure for each — New leads, Sales value, Deliveries and Services completed.
Press **Save targets**.

body.text: Leave one blank to have no target for it this month; its card then shows just the running figure.
Targets are set month by month, so set next month's at the start of the month.

title: Reading the sales forecast
summary: How much is likely to close this month, filtered by pipeline, team and person.

body.text: The **Sales forecast** shows the open deals expected to close in a month and how much they're likely to be worth. You need the **View sales forecasts** permission, and you see only the leads, teams and people you're allowed to.
Filtering
Choose the **Period** (month), **Pipeline**, **Team** and **Owner**, then press **Apply**.
The figures

rows: The total value of open deals
Each deal's value times its chance of winning, added up — the realistic figure
Deals the team is confident will close
Deals that could close if things go well

body.text: The table lists each open lead with its pipeline and stage, owner and team, expected close date, forecast category, chance of winning, value and weighted value.

title: Adjusting forecast deals and capturing snapshots
summary: Managers set each deal's chance of winning, category and close date, and save the forecast for the record.

body.text: With the **Update forecast categories, probabilities and close dates** permission you can fine-tune each deal and save snapshots of the forecast.
Editing a deal

items: In the forecast table, press **Edit** on a lead's row.
Set the **probability** (0–100).
Choose a **forecast category**: Pipeline, Best case, Commit or Omitted.
Set the **expected close date** and, if you like, an **estimated cost**.
If you can assign leads, set the **team**. Save.

body.text: The category decides which figure a deal counts towards — **Commit** deals count in the Commit total, and **Omitted** deals are left out.
Capturing a snapshot

Press **Capture snapshot** to save the forecast as it is now, for the chosen period, pipeline, team and person. Recent snapshots are listed at the bottom with their open value, weighted value, number of deals and when they were taken — useful for comparing how the month went against what was expected.

title: Tracking and rewarding referrals
summary: Follow customers' introductions from referral code to won deal, and record the reward when it's given.

body.text: The **Referrals** page follows customer introductions from a referral code to a won deal and the reward. Every customer has one permanent **referral code** on their profile — three letters from your business name and four characters, for example ACM-K7PQ.
How a referral moves along

rows: Someone was introduced; no deal won yet
The referred deal was won — the reward is owed

body.text: When a new lead comes in with a customer's code, it's linked to that customer. When the deal is won, the referral becomes **fee due** by itself. Someone using their own code, or a code that doesn't exist, is simply ignored — a typo never stops a lead coming in.
Recording the reward

items: Find the referral marked **fee due**.
In **Reward provided**, note what was given — for example a voucher.
Press **Mark reward redeemed**.

body.text: The cards at the top count rewards due, introductions in progress and rewards given. Recording a reward needs the **Create, earn and redeem referrals** permission.
